_comment: Loading-screen quotes. Only well-attested words with the work they come from; no apocrypha. Translations are public domain (named where the wording follows one). Add more in the same shape.

quotes.text: All warfare is based on deception.
quotes.source: The Art of War I.18, trans. Lionel Giles (1910)

quotes.text: Supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting.
quotes.source: The Art of War III.2, trans. Lionel Giles (1910)

quotes.text: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
quotes.source: The Art of War III.18, trans. Lionel Giles (1910)

quotes.text: Appear at points which the enemy must hasten to defend; march swiftly to places where you are not expected.
quotes.source: The Art of War VI.5, trans. Lionel Giles (1910)

quotes.text: All Gaul is divided into three parts.
quotes.source: Commentaries on the Gallic War I.1

quotes.text: The die is cast.
quotes.source: at the Rubicon, 49 BC; Suetonius, Life of Julius Caesar 32

quotes.text: I came, I saw, I conquered.
quotes.source: after Zela, 47 BC; Suetonius, Life of Julius Caesar 37

quotes.text: The sinews of war: money without limit.
quotes.source: Philippics V.5

quotes.text: In time of war the laws fall silent.
quotes.source: Pro Milone 11

quotes.text: Make haste slowly.
quotes.source: Suetonius, Life of Augustus 25 (festina lente)

quotes.text: If I were not Alexander, I would be Diogenes.
quotes.source: Plutarch, Life of Alexander 14

quotes.text: If we are victorious in one more battle with the Romans, we shall be utterly ruined.
quotes.source: Plutarch, Life of Pyrrhus 21, trans. Bernadotte Perrin (1920)

quotes.text: The strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must.
quotes.source: History of the Peloponnesian War V.89 (the Melian dialogue), trans. Richard Crawley (1874)

quotes.text: The sea! The sea!
quotes.source: Anabasis IV.7.24, the Ten Thousand sighting the Black Sea

quotes.text: War is the father of all and the king of all.
quotes.source: Fragment B53, trans. John Burnet (1920)

quotes.text: They make a solitude and call it peace.
quotes.source: Agricola 30 (the speech of Calgacus), trans. Church and Brodribb (1877)

quotes.text: He, therefore, who desires peace, should prepare for war.
quotes.source: De Re Militari, preface to Book III, trans. John Clarke (1767)

quotes.text: Give me a place to stand, and I will move the earth.
quotes.source: Pappus of Alexandria, Collection VIII

quotes.text: It is much safer to be feared than loved, when, of the two, either must be dispensed with.
quotes.source: The Prince, ch. 17, trans. W. K. Marriott (1908)

quotes.text: A prince ought to have no other aim or thought, nor select anything else for his study, than war and its rules and discipline.
quotes.source: The Prince, ch. 14, trans. W. K. Marriott (1908)

quotes.text: From the sublime to the ridiculous there is but one step.
quotes.source: to the Abbé de Pradt in Warsaw, December 1812; de Pradt, Histoire de l'ambassade dans le grand-duché de Varsovie (1815)

quotes.text: I, whose ambition leads me not only farther than any other man has been before me, but as far as I think it possible for man to go.
quotes.source: journal, 30 January 1774, at his farthest south

quotes.text: War is a mere continuation of policy by other means.
quotes.source: On War I.1.24, trans. J. J. Graham (1873)

quotes.text: Everything is very simple in War, but the simplest thing is difficult.
quotes.source: On War I.7, trans. J. J. Graham (1873)

quotes.text: No plan of operations extends with any certainty beyond the first contact with the main hostile force.
quotes.source: Über Strategie (1871)

quotes.text: A house divided against itself cannot stand.
quotes.source: House Divided speech, Springfield, 16 June 1858

quotes.text: With malice toward none, with charity for all.
quotes.source: Second Inaugural Address, 4 March 1865
